vo.en: Stop touching things in the store.

visual.description: A close-up shot of a man's hand reaching out to grab a premium leather wallet on a display shelf.

vo.en: Retailers know that if you hold an item for just thirty seconds, your brain flips a switch.

visual.description: A digital stopwatch counting up rapidly overlaying a man holding a high-end camera.

vo.en: Suddenly, you don't just want it. You feel like you already own it. This is the Endowment Effect.

visual.description: A man looking at a product in his hands with a look of deep satisfaction and personal connection.

vo.en: But here is the creepy part: putting it back actually triggers physical pain in your brain.

visual.description: Slow motion shot of a man reluctantly placing a box back onto a store shelf and pulling his hand away.

vo.en: Try it now. Pick up your phone or a nearby mug. Hold it. Feel that shift in value? That's the trap.

visual.description: A man's hand lifting a ceramic coffee mug from a wooden desk in a cozy office setting.

vo.en: Subscribe for more brain hacks—and comment GOT ME if you felt that ownership shift, which is exactly why

visual.description: A close-up of a finger clicking the subscribe button on a screen followed by a man nodding at the camera.
